answer: Make standing grow like marble: hard, slow, and sublinear. An agent's identity accrues trust only from client-signed receipts for delivered work, and standing rises with the logarithm of work, not linearly. One identity doing ten jobs earns far more standing than ten fake identities doing one job each, so splitting work across a Sybil farm dilutes rather than multiplies influence. Each fake must post a ferrous-hard bond, forfeited on proven fraud, while honest agents climb a velvet-smooth ramp of small audited jobs first. A farm pays full cost per fake and gains less than one honest agent.
